title: Canonical identity scalar quotient-completion chain unit
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with its fixed valuation ring and uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $Y$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_E=\varprojlim_{n\ge0}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the identity-extension quotient tower $T(P)$ and its strict Roos complex $C(P)$ for every unbounded complex $P$ of $R_E$-module sheaves [def-trf-integral-scalar-tower-functors]. In the mapping-cocone coordinates $C(P)^i=(\prod_nT(P)_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_nT(P)_n^i)$ [def-sf-strict-roos-functor], define the canonical natural chain map $\eta:\operatorname{Id}\to C$ to be the unique map with zero shifted coordinate and whose unshifted coordinate, after every product projection, sends every section $x\in P^i(U)$ to the sheafified tensor section $1\otimes x\in T(P)_n^i(U)$. Its existence and uniqueness are the already proved constructor theorem completedScalarIdentityUnit_existsUnique; completedScalarIdentityUnit is its unique selected map. There is no K-flatness, completeness, constructibility or boundedness condition on $P$, and the scheme and coefficient universes are independent. This definition is before localization and assumes no finite-free completed scalar comparison theorem.
